section_title: Phase 2 adjudication, net rates by SOP class
claim: dciodvfy's Error on a missing Laterality (0020,0060) in the General Series Module is a validator floor, not a conformance defect, because the Type 2C condition cannot be evaluated from the dataset and PS3.5 makes absence mandatory when the condition is not met.
status_note: Verified against the standard text, not measured. This is the single adjudication that decides the Error-severity result for 462 of the 1,086 objects, so the condition is quoted verbatim in the source file so a reader can check it.
value: PS3.3 Table C.7-5a, Laterality (0020,0060), Type 2C: "Laterality of (paired) body part examined. Required if the body part examined is a paired structure and Image Laterality (0020,0062) or Frame Laterality (0020,9072) or Measurement Laterality (0024,0113) are not present." PS3.5 7.4.4: "It is a protocol violation if the specified conditions are met and the Data Element is not included. When the specified conditions are not met, Type 2C Data Elements shall not be included in the Data Set unless it is specified that they may be present otherwise." Verdict FLOOR, 1 message class, 462 objects.
floor: this row is a floor determination, so it has no rate of its own. The identical message class id e4c7fa2d56f7 is already in results/floor_set.csv against a known-good Parametric Map built by highdicom, which is the empirical form of the same point.
external_source: PS3.3 2026c C.7.3.1 General Series Module, Table C.7-5a; PS3.5 2026c 7.4.4 Type 2C Conditional Data Elements; PS3.3 2026c C.11.9 Table C.11.9-1 Presentation Series Module; PS3.3 2026c A.33.1 Table A.33.1-1
notes: Three facts carry it. The condition's trigger is whether the body part examined is a paired structure, and Body Part Examined (0018,0015) is Type 3 in the same Table C.7-5a, so a conformant object need not carry it. PS3.3 publishes no normative list of paired body parts, so a present value would still not settle the condition by citation. PS3.5 7.4.4 makes the two readings symmetric, so the same message covers a violation and mandatory compliance. The Presentation Series Module, which PS3.3 A.33.1 names as specialising General Series for this IOD, specialises only Modality (0008,0060) and leaves Laterality at Type 2C. This does not say the objects have no laterality problem. It says the standard's text does not let a third party score one from the dataset.

section_title: Phase 2 adjudication, net rates by SOP class
claim: dciodvfy's "Value dubious for this VR, Retired Person Name form" warning has no conformance requirement behind it. PS3.5 explicitly permits a PN value with a single component and no delimiter.
status_note: Verified against the standard text. Recorded as PLAUSIBILITY rather than FLOOR because the complaint is about the shape of a value rather than about a construct the IOD tables permit, and the rubric names this message as the canonical plausibility case.
value: PS3.5 Table 6.2-1, PN: "Any of the five components may be an empty string. The component delimiter shall be the caret \"^\" character (5EH). There shall be no more than four component delimiters, i.e., none after the last component if all components are present. Delimiters are required for interior null components. Trailing null components and their delimiters may be omitted." Verdict PLAUSIBILITY, 34 message classes, 1,086 objects.
floor: this row is a plausibility determination, so it has no rate of its own
external_source: PS3.5 2026c 6.2 Value Representation, Table 6.2-1, row PN Person Name
notes: 34 distinct message classes for one finding, because the patient name is inside the message text and the census keys a class on the normalised text. Every one of the 34 has its own row in results/phase2/adjudication_gsps.csv. None is skipped. The values are collection and case identifiers such as QIBA_CT_1C and UID rather than person names, which is a de-identification artefact and not a conformance question.

section_title: Phase 2 adjudication, net rates by SOP class
claim: dciodvfy's DisplayedAreaSelectionSequence ordering check has no located requirement behind it in PS3.3 or PS3.4, so it is recorded as plausibility. This adjudication is contested and it decides the PRE-05 outcome for this class, so both readings are reported.
status_note: CONTESTED. PS3.3 C.10.4 and Table C.10-4 were read in full and PS3.4 Annex N was checked. Neither states an ordering relation between the two corners, neither uses shall for one, and neither forbids a region one column or one row wide. NET is refused because the rubric requires a section and table giving the Type or condition violated and no such text was located. FLOOR is refused because nothing cited positively permits a degenerate region either. The counterfactual is reported rather than suppressed.
value: PS3.3 Table C.10-4: Displayed Area Top Left Hand Corner (0070,0052) and Bottom Right Hand Corner (0070,0053) are both Type 1 and both present with values valid for VR SL and VM 2. Note in C.10.4: "The TLHC and BRHC may be outside the boundaries of the image pixel data (e.g., the TLHC may be 0 or negative, or the BRHC may be greater than Rows or Columns), allowing minification or placement of the image pixel data within a larger Specified Displayed Area." Verdict PLAUSIBILITY, 135 message classes, 152 objects. Counterfactual if read as NET: Error gross 513, floor 361, net 152, class net rate 14.00 percent, collection-level median net rate 10.68 percent.
floor: under the recorded verdict this class is part of the floor and the class net Error rate is 0.00 percent. Under the counterfactual the class net Error rate is 14.00 percent and the Error floor drops from 513 to 361 objects.
external_source: PS3.3 2026c C.10.4 Displayed Area Module, Table C.10-4; PS3.4 2026c Annex N Softcopy Presentation State Storage SOP Classes; PS3.5 2026c 7.4.1 Type 1 Required Data Elements
notes: In every observed message one axis is equal rather than inverted, for example TopLeft = (344,0) against BottomRight = (344,512), so dciodvfy applies a strict inequality on both axes that the standard does not state. A reader who holds that the words top left and bottom right in an Attribute Description are themselves normative moves this class to NET, which makes the class rate 14.00 percent and the collection median 10.68 percent, both above 5.0 percent. Under PRE-05's own three-band wording that counterfactual is indeterminate rather than substantial, because it is below 20 percent. This row exists so that reading is on the record and not reachable only by recomputation.

section_title: Phase 2 adjudication, net rates by SOP class
claim: Evaluated against PRE-05, the Grayscale Softcopy Presentation State class is not substantial. Both the class net Error-class rate and the collection-level median net Error rate are zero.
status_note: PRE-05 itself is not touched by this track. It is defined per object class and three sibling tracks adjudicate the other complete classes against the same row id, so writing an outcome into PRE-05 from one class would either overwrite a sibling's outcome or destroy the threshold definition its value field carries. The outcome is recorded here instead, with PRE-05 named in derived_from, for the orchestrator to consolidate once all complete classes have landed.
value: net Error-class rate 0.00 percent, 0 of 1,086, does not exceed 5.0 percent. Collection-level median net Error rate 0.00 percent, does not exceed 5.0 percent. Substantial requires both. Verdict: not substantial. Against PRE-05's own three-band wording, 0.00 percent is at or below 5 percent, which PRE-05 calls null, so PRE-01's prediction of a largely null Claim 1 is not contradicted by this class.
floor: gross Error-class rate 47.24 percent, all of it floor, NOT-IOD or plausibility. Net 0.00 percent. The rate is quoted with its floor because without the floor the 47.24 percent gross number would read as a failure rate.

Under the contested-class counterfactual of C-GSPS-07 the two numbers become 14.00 percent and 10.68 percent, both above 5.0 percent, which would read substantial on the two-rate rule and indeterminate on PRE-05's own three-band rule. That is stated here rather than left in the source file.
